fixtures.response:
A system prompt is the standing instruction set that defines the model's role, tone, and rules for a whole conversation — it's sent once and applies to every turn. The user message is the specific request; the system prompt is the frame around it. In a product, engineering usually owns the system prompt (it encodes policy and guardrails) while the user controls the messages.

Streaming sends the response token-by-token as the model generates it, instead of waiting for the whole reply. It doesn't make the model faster — total generation time is the same — but it makes the interface *feel* fast, because the user sees words appearing within a few hundred milliseconds instead of staring at a spinner. It cuts perceived latency, not actual latency.
